source.title: The lost key (ladder unit, machine-drafted)
source.author: Go course authors (drafted by an AI model)

source.provenance: Drafted by an AI model for the course ladder in simple Ecclesiastical (Church) Latin; not reviewed by a Latinist. It is controlled, deliberately repetitive Latin written for learners and may contain unidiomatic phrasing. The English lines are the drafter's own.

review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting review by a Latinist. House style: simple Church Latin, spelled without macrons, with u/v and i/j as in Stage 0 (v and i only); present tense, with a few perfects (venit, vidit, fuit, dixit) in the last units.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Hodie Marcus clavem non habet. Clavis est clavis domus Marthae.
sentences.english: Today Marcus does not have the key. It is the key of Martha's house.

sentences.text: Marcus fessus est. Domum venire vult, sed clavem non habet.
sentences.english: Marcus is tired. He wants to come home, but he does not have the key.

sentences.text: Ubi est clavis mea? Clavem non habeo!
sentences.english: Where is my key? I do not have the key!
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Marcus clavem quaerit. In schola clavem quaerit. Clavis in schola non est.
sentences.english: Marcus looks for the key. He looks for the key at school. The key is not at school.

sentences.text: Marcus in foro clavem quaerit. Clavis in foro non est.
sentences.english: Marcus looks for the key in the market. The key is not in the market.

sentences.text: Samuel Marcum videt. Samuel puerum salutat.
sentences.english: Samuel sees Marcus. Samuel greets the boy.

sentences.text: Salve, Marce! Quid quaeris?
sentences.english: Hello, Marcus! What are you looking for?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Clavem quaero. Clavem non habeo. Fessus sum, et domum venire volo.
sentences.english: I am looking for the key. I do not have the key. I am tired, and I want to come home.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Ego te iuvo! Ubi clavem quaeris?
sentences.english: I will help you! Where are you looking for the key?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: In schola quaero, et in foro quaero. Clavis ibi non est.
sentences.english: I look at school, and I look in the market. The key is not there.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Estne in ecclesia? Quaerimus in ecclesia!
sentences.english: Is it in the church? Let us look in the church!
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Samuel et Marcus in ecclesia clavem quaerunt. Clavis ibi non est.
sentences.english: Samuel and Marcus look for the key in the church. The key is not there.

sentences.text: Clavis hic non est. Non invenimus!
sentences.english: The key is not here. We do not find it!
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Ubi est Martha? Martha clavem habet?
sentences.english: Where is Martha? Does Martha have the key?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Martha in domo est. Sed domus clavem non habet. Clavis mea est!
sentences.english: Martha is at home. But the house does not have the key. The key is mine!
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Veni! In domum Marthae venimus.
sentences.english: Come! We come to Martha's house.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Martha in porta est. Marcum et Samuelem videt.
sentences.english: Martha is at the door. She sees Marcus and Samuel.

sentences.text: Salvete! Quid hic facitis? Quid quaeritis?
sentences.english: Hello! What are you doing here? What are you looking for?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Clavem quaerimus, avia. Clavem meam non habeo.
sentences.english: We are looking for the key, grandmother. I do not have my key.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Ecce clavis! Clavis in mensa est, sub pane. Statim clavem video.
sentences.english: Look, the key! The key is on the table, under the bread. I see the key at once.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Ibi est! Clavem tandem invenio!
sentences.english: It is there! At last I find the key!
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Bene est, Marce! Clavem habes. Tandem clavem invenis.
sentences.english: It is well, Marcus! You have the key. At last you find the key.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago, Samuel. Gratias tibi ago, avia. Tu amicus bonus es.
sentences.english: Thank you, Samuel. Thank you, grandmother. You are a good friend.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Statim panem edite! Panis sub mensa non est, sed in mensa est.
sentences.english: Eat bread at once! The bread is not under the table, but on the table.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Marcus clavem in manu habet. Ibi panem edit, et lac bibit. Tandem fessus non est.
sentences.english: Marcus has the key in his hand. There he eats bread, and drinks milk. At last he is not tired.

sentences.text: Samuel quoque panem edit. Bene est. Hodie Samuel Marcum iuvat, et Marcus Samuelem iuvat.
sentences.english: Samuel eats bread too. It is well. Today Samuel helps Marcus, and Marcus helps Samuel.
